title: Fit a shaft-end magnetic encoder and verify its installation
instruction: Install the magnetic encoder on the motor shaft. Seat the magnet carrier, lower the sensor bracket onto its guide posts, and close its retaining catch. Press the field-test button, then release the assembly.
context: Magnetic robot-joint encoders rely on a centred, retained magnet and a fixed gap to a secured sensor. The fit can be checked before powering the motor.
setup: An unpowered Ø80 mm motor with an 8 mm steel D-shaft with an axial detent groove is fixed to a tabletop fixture. The magnetic carrier with a 20 × 20 mm grasp flange, keyed bore and spring ball plunger and the PCB bracket start separately in docks. Two guide posts 76 mm apart set the bracket position and nominal 1.5 mm sensor gap. A red catch starts outboard of the bracket, and the field-test LED starts off.
scoring: 0.25 for the released keyed carrier within 0.65 mm of its datum and 11.5° of the flat. 0.45 if the bracket seats on both guides, 0.65 if its catch retains it. Full score requires the field check and key release, both hands clear, and at most 0.50 mm of carrier lift under a 2.0 N axial proof load for 0.30 s.
fidelity: Native rigid-body collisions drive grasping and insertion against the D-flat. A reduced-order spring plunger engages the shaft groove. A 2.0 N upward proof load acts on the native carrier body and the scorer measures its displacement. The catch and field key use native sliders. The simulated field check uses measured fit. The physical fixture uses an AS5600 diagnostic and a spring scale.
scores: Dream-1: 0.00 in 1,400 steps. Scripted YAM: 1.00 in 601 steps.
